Generate a smooth centerline with a flat interaction segment

Source: R/centerline.R
generate_centerline.Rd

Assembles a single reference mean-pathway by integrating a tangent-angle field over arc length. The central interaction segment is exactly straight for interaction_length units; the two equal arms bend smoothly (C1) by angle (radians). The result is already parametrized by curvilinear arc length and is discretized onto n_points equally spaced points (via fiber::reparametrize()).

Usage

generate_centerline(
  angle = 0.5,
  arm_length = 1,
  interaction_length = 2,
  rotation = 0,
  vertical_bend = 0,
  n_points = 1000L
)

Arguments

angle

Bending angle (radians) reached by each arm. Bounded to (-pi/2, pi/2).

arm_length

Length (in output units) of each straight run of the bending arms that lead up to the flat central segment. Together with interaction_length it sets how far the arms extend.

interaction_length

Length of the flat central (straight) part of the centreline, in the same units as the output points.

rotation

Rotation (radians) applied to the whole centreline about the vertical (Y) axis after generation. Defaults to 0.

vertical_bend

Optional bend angle (radians) applied out of the xy-plane (towards z), so the centreline can tile a truly 3-D fascicle. Defaults to 0 (a planar centreline).

n_points

Number of equally spaced points on the grid (in curvilinear arc length). Defaults to 1000.

Value

A n_points x 3 numeric matrix with column names X, Y, Z giving the arc-length-parametrized centreline.

Examples

cl <- generate_centerline(angle = 0.6, arm_length = 1,
                          interaction_length = 2, n_points = 200)
colnames(cl) # c("X", "Y", "Z")
#> [1] "X" "Y" "Z"
nrow(cl)     # 200
#> [1] 200
